The faction has also declared support for former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, ahead of the 2027 general election, accusing those who endorsed President Tinubu of making a political decision without consulting communities and other stakeholders across the Middle Belt.
The disagreement follows a November 5 visit by a delegation led by Gen Danjuma to President Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where they discussed political cooperation, security and support for the president ahead of the 2027 election.
The delegation included Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang, his Taraba State counterpart Agbu Kefas, Defence Minister Christopher Musa, APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda, former Speaker of the House of Representatives Yakubu Dogara, former Chief of Army Staff Ishaya Bamaiyi, businessman Thomas Etuh and Pogu Bitrus.
Mr Dogara subsequently told journalists that the delegation visited to demonstrate solidarity with the president and discuss ways of mobilising support for his administration.
Gen Danjuma later publicly endorsed Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid at the 20th anniversary and fundraising ceremony of the Adamawa State Government House Chapel in Yola.
Represented by Mr Bamaiyi, the retired general urged Nigerians, particularly people from the Middle Belt, to support Mr Tinubu, arguing that another four years would enable the president to consolidate on projects initiated by his administration.
He also cited the appointment of Christians into key government positions as evidence of the president’s fairness and religious tolerance.
However, the endorsement has triggered opposition from a faction of the Middle Belt Forum, which says neither Mr Danjuma nor the delegation had the mandate to commit the region to a political candidate.
Addressing newsmen in Jos, the coordinator of the Big 10 Coalition North Central, Emmanuel Zopmal, said the meeting at the Presidential Villa was not representative of the Middle Belt because it excluded several stakeholders and political interests.
The spokesperson argued that the presence of the APC national chairman at the meeting raised questions about whether it was a regional consultation or an engagement involving APC-aligned politicians.
“If it is truly a Middle Belt meeting, why were other Middle Belters who are national chairmen of other political parties not involved?” he asked.
The coalition said the region’s political future should not be determined by a handful of individuals in Abuja without consulting its communities, elders, youths and other stakeholders.
It therefore appealed to Gen Danjuma to reconsider his position and withdraw the reported endorsement.
The group said its opposition was informed by what it described as the Tinubu administration’s failure to adequately address insecurity, displacement and the loss of ancestral lands across the Middle Belt.
It argued that millions of residents displaced by attacks had yet to return to their communities, while several affected areas remained unrecovered.
The coalition also accused the president of neglecting communities affected by violence, citing his failure to visit Angware-Kuba in Plateau State following the Palm Sunday killings.
It alleged that President Tinubu stopped at the airport during the visit, citing a lack of electricity as the reason he could not proceed to the affected community.
The group contrasted that episode with the president’s campaign visits, arguing that the situation demonstrated a lack of concern for the people whose votes he would seek in 2027.
It also questioned the federal government’s record on infrastructure in the region, particularly the failure to upgrade Yakubu Gowon Airport in Jos, Plateau State.
The coalition said residents of Plateau often had to travel to Gombe State to access international flights, describing the situation as evidence of inadequate federal presence.
Explaining its preference for Mr Obi, the coalition said the former Anambra State governor had demonstrated empathy towards communities affected by insecurity even before declaring his presidential ambition.
It cited his intervention during the killings in Benue State in 2016, when, according to the spokesperson, Mr Obi personally assigned him to deliver relief materials to victims through the then governor, Samuel Ortom.
The disagreement over Mr Tinubu’s endorsement has also exposed a deepening leadership crisis within the Middle Belt Forum, with some state chairmen announcing a vote of no confidence in its president, Bitrus Pogu.
Notsa Bello, the Taraba State chairman of the forum, said state chairmen from 14 states had passed the resolution at a meeting in Nasarawa State on Tuesday.
Mr Bello accused Mr Pogu of running the organisation for eight years without conducting elections, holding congresses or providing accountability to its members.
